page_numbering: Printed page numbers match one-based PDF page indices. HTML/PDF #page=N references target these numbers.
scope: Simplified DearFlow lead agent with all 14 middleware enabled; source and installed LangChain were read without edits or network calls.

stages.title: Before the agent starts
stages.frequency: Normally once when this graph invocation begins, not again after every tool call.
stages.explanation: Prepare the shared conversation state: add a current-date reminder and saved user facts when needed.
stages.before: The user message and any existing conversation state.
stages.after: A state patch adds hidden date and memory messages; the next stage sees the updated state.
stages.compare: Input.before.value → Output.state_update.value, then inspect the next hook input for the merged state.

stages.title: Before each model attempt
stages.frequency: Each ordinary model-loop iteration, including after ordinary tool results and Todo reroutes.
stages.explanation: Update the shared state before constructing the model request. Shorten older conversation if the threshold is crossed; restore a saved todo reminder if its original context disappeared.
stages.before: Current state, including previous tool results and saved todos.
stages.after: A state patch may replace old history with a summary or append a hidden todo reminder; null means no patch.
stages.compare: Input.before.value → Output.state_update.value. The patch is not the full model request.

stages.title: Around the model request and reply
stages.frequency: Each main-model call. Wrappers nest; entering and returning are two sides of the same operation.
stages.explanation: On entry, layers prepare a temporary request copy: receipts, user boundaries, repaired tool history, budget warning, loop warning, todo system instructions, then personal-data masking. On return, the same layers unwind in reverse; ToolReceipt stamps the ledger on the returned AI message.
stages.before: A request containing the current messages, system instructions, available tools and settings.
stages.after: The innermost model gets the final prepared request. The outer layers receive the returned AI message; most do not rewrite the reply.
stages.compare: Entry: Input.before.value → Output.calls[0].request.value. Return: Output.calls[0].response.value → Output.result.value. Later inner wrappers may further change the request.

stages.title: The model generates one reply
stages.frequency: One actual LLM invocation; a user turn can contain many.
stages.explanation: The provider receives the fully assembled request and generates text, tool requests, and token usage. A generated tool request describes a proposed action; it has not executed yet.
stages.before: Final system instructions, eligible messages and provider tool definitions.
stages.after: AI text and/or tool_calls, with usage_metadata.
stages.compare: Select the innermost ChatOpenAI LLM span and compare Input with Output. Count actual LLM spans, not surrounding middleware spans.

stages.title: Inspect the generated reply
stages.frequency: After a model reply, until any explicit routing jump changes the path.
stages.explanation: Reverse registration order. Clarification removes sibling actions when asking the user; Todo can ask the model to continue; loop and budget guards can remove tool requests; the delegation guard trims excess task calls.
stages.before: State with the newly generated AI message.
stages.after: A patch may replace that AI message, add a reminder, or set jump_to. Requested tools only execute after the guards permit them.
stages.compare: Input.before.value → Output.state_update.value. Same message id means replacement, not an additional answer.
stages.routing_note: The displayed order is the normal sequence. Todo jump_to=model resolves to the loop entry (before_model), so it can skip later after_model hooks in that iteration.

stages.title: Around each permitted tool call
stages.frequency: Once per tool execution/interception; a model reply can request multiple tools.
stages.explanation: Clarification can supply a question without invoking the underlying tool. For an ordinary tool, the inner handler runs it; selected external outputs are masked; ordinary failures become error results; the outer receipt layer stamps the final result.
stages.before: One permitted tool call, including its name, arguments and call id.
stages.after: A ToolMessage, or a Command carrying a result and routing/state update. Ordinary results return to before_model; return_direct clarification proceeds to after_agent.
stages.compare: Input.before.value and Output.calls/result. handler_calls=0 is expected for intercepted ask_clarification.
stages.exception_note: When an inner handler raises, PII does not receive a normal result on that path. ToolErrorHandling catches the exception outside it and creates an error ToolMessage; ToolReceipt then stamps that result.

stages.title: After the agent finishes this invocation
stages.frequency: Normally once on the graph completion path, after the model/tool loop ends; ordinary unhandled errors can prevent normal completion.
stages.explanation: Title writes a short conversation label. Memory queues the latest real user/assistant exchange for later fact extraction. They are completion work, not another pass over every model reply.
stages.before: Completed turn state and the final exchange.
stages.after: A title state patch may appear; memory normally returns null while queuing a side effect. Later background extraction and disk persistence require separate verification.
stages.compare: For Title compare Input.before.value → Output.state_update.value. For Memory, null is expected; verify accepted saved facts and recall in a later fresh thread.

pitfalls: A user turn is one RunService/user request; agent means the compiled loop handling it. Model means one provider call inside that loop. Tool calls are proposed by the model and executed later.
Before/after agent delimit normal graph execution. Before/after model repeat around model attempts. They are not four middleware functions that every component must implement.

Middleware registration order is not one flat list executed uniformly. Each hook selects only components that implement it. before hooks run forward; after hooks run backward; wrappers enter forward and return backward.
Todo inherits wrap_model_call from LangChain TodoListMiddleware, and RedactingSummarization inherits before_model from SummarizationMiddleware. Searching only local def lines would miss these hooks.
A wrapper return transformation happens before the graph after_model hooks. ToolReceipt stamping on the returning AI message is therefore not itself an after_model hook.

State patches and request overrides differ: date, memory, summary and todo reminders change graph state; sanitation, repaired history, receipt ledger, warning messages and user-text PII masking usually alter a request copy. The original stored user text is not necessarily rewritten.
The reply’s tool_calls are requests, not receipts. Guards can remove them. Actual completed ToolMessages and stamped receipts show what executed.

The ordinary tool-return path loops to before_model, not before_agent. ask_clarification is return_direct and completes through after_agent, and the next user reply creates a new run on the same thread.

Todo jump_to=model maps to the loop entry (before_model) in installed LangChain and may bypass later after_model hooks that iteration. Clarification disabled uses a Command(goto="model"), a direct graph-node jump; distinguish it from middleware jump_to.

After_agent Memory queues background work. A successful span or null state_update does not mean facts are saved. Acknowledgment text is not memory proof; accepted saved facts and a later answer without supplied facts are stronger evidence.
Not every enabled hook changes data. A no-op can be correct when no threshold, sensitive text, broken history or pending work needs handling.
Metadata labels such as dearflow_hook, langgraph_step and ls_run_depth describe tracing. They do not automatically enter the model prompt.
Never sum parent wrapper token totals with child LLM totals. Count each real LLM call once; background memory extraction can be outside the user-turn trace.
PII export redaction_applied is a snapshot-export flag. It is not the runtime PiiRedactionMiddleware verdict. The full guide documents the paired evidence and limitations.
The exact normal lead chain has 14 components, but subagents use a smaller chain. The companion must not imply each subagent repeats all lead hooks.

source_references.description: First registered component is the outermost wrapper.
create_agent receives the instrumented middleware chain.
Graph entry, loop-entry, loop-exit and completion nodes.
Tools loop to before_model, except return_direct and structured output completion.
after_model and after_agent hooks run in reverse registration order.
jump_to=model resolves to supplied loop-entry destination.
Todo completion reminder and jump_to=model; inherited wrapper adds instructions.
Disabled clarification uses Command goto=model; enabled clarification is intercepted.
after_agent enqueues extraction and returns None.
